questions.question: What belongs among a person’s basic needs?
questions.explanation: Basic needs are essential things required for survival, like nourishment, protection, and clothing.

questions.question: Why do we need food and water?
options: So that we have more things at home
So that the body functions properly and has energy
So that we can sleep more
questions.explanation: Food and water provide the fuel and hydration necessary for our bodies to work and stay healthy.

questions.question: What does the word “needs” mean?
options: Things we want to have for fun
Things without which we are still able to function
Things that we need to live
Things that we buy once a year
questions.explanation: Needs are necessities that are vital for our existence and well-being.

questions.question: Why is housing important?
options: So that we have a place to store toys
It gives us safety and a place to rest
Housing is nice, and people need it because they like it
questions.explanation: A home provides shelter from the elements, security, and a space for recovery.

questions.question: Chrumko goes to the shop and has little money. What should he buy first?
questions.explanation: When money is limited, you should always prioritize needs (food) over wants (chocolate or toys).

questions.question: Chrumko only buys sweets and no longer has money for food. What does that mean?
options: He chose a want over a need
questions.explanation: Sweets are a luxury (want), while food is a necessity (need). Chrumko prioritized the wrong thing.

questions.question: Which kind of thing is a want?
options: Something without which we cannot live
Something we want but do not need
Something we must have every day
questions.explanation: A want is something that makes life more pleasant but isn't required for survival.

questions.question: Which of the following is a want?
questions.explanation: A stuffed toy is for entertainment, unlike water, food, and housing which are essential.

questions.question: How are needs and wants different?
options: Wants are more important than needs
Needs are necessary, wants are not
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: The main difference is necessity; you must have needs to survive, but you can live without wants.

questions.question: Is it okay to have wants?
options: Yes, but we should know that needs are more important
No, we should only buy needs
Yes, and we should always fulfil them immediately
questions.explanation: Wants are fine to have, as long as your basic needs are met first.

questions.question: Chrumko wants a new toy, but he already has a similar one at home. What does that mean?
questions.explanation: Since he already has a toy that works, the new one is definitely a desire, not a necessity.

questions.question: Chrumko has money only for one thing. What should he do?
options: Always buy the most expensive thing
First consider what he really needs
Do not spend the money at all
questions.explanation: Responsible money management means checking if your needs are covered before spending on anything else.

lessons.lessonName: Why we want things we do not need

questions.question: Why do we want some things immediately when we see them?
options: Because the brain associates them with a feeling of joy
questions.explanation: Our brains often react to cool or shiny things by promising us a feeling of happiness if we get them.

questions.question: What can influence our desire for something?
questions.explanation: We often want things because we see them in commercials or because our friends have them.

questions.question: If we want something, does that mean we also need it?
questions.explanation: Wanting something and needing something are two different feelings.

questions.question: What is good to do before buying something?
options: Make sure it is in fashion
questions.explanation: Taking a 'cooling off' period helps you decide if you really want the item or if it was just a quick impulse.

questions.question: Chrumko wants a new pencil case, but his old one still works. What is true?
options: Chrumko should throw the old pencil case away
questions.explanation: If the current item still performs its function, a new one is a want.

questions.question: Chrumko wants a new pencil case, but his old one still works. He thinks about it and does not buy the pencil case. Why?
options: He realized that he does not need it
The pencil case disappeared from the shop
questions.explanation: By thinking it over, Chrumko practiced good financial discipline by identifying it as an unnecessary want.

questions.question: Why does advertising exist?
options: So that people want to buy the product
To give us more free time
So that the person who buys the product earns money
questions.explanation: The primary goal of advertising is to persuade people to spend money on a specific product.

questions.question: How does advertising make things more attractive?
options: It uses colors, music, and pictures
It does not; it only shows them to people
questions.explanation: Ads use sensory tricks to make products look and sound better than they might actually be.

questions.question: Are things in ads always the same as in reality?
options: Yes, the product being advertised does not exist
No, they can look worse than in reality
Yes, they never contain any true information about the product
No, but they are usually exaggerated or misleading
questions.explanation: Advertisers often show the 'perfect' version of a product, which can be different from what you actually get.

questions.question: What should we look at when choosing a product?
options: Mainly what it contains and whether we need it
questions.explanation: Smart shoppers look at the quality and the necessity of the item rather than the flashy packaging.

questions.question: Chrumko sees a big chocolate bar in an ad, but in the shop it is smaller. Why?
options: The ad made it look more attractive
There was a mistake when they put it into the shop
questions.explanation: This is a common advertising tactic to make the product seem like a better deal than it is.

questions.question: Chrumko wants to buy something just because he saw it in an ad. What should he do?
options: Immediately find it and buy it
Ignore it because ads always lie
Think about whether he really needs it
questions.explanation: You should always check if the desire comes from an actual need or just the influence of a clever ad.

questions.question: When do people often buy things without thinking?
options: When they are tired or angry
When they are calm and relaxed
When they have made a shopping list of needed items
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can cloud our judgment and make us make impulsive purchases.

questions.question: Why do we sometimes buy things when we are sad?
options: Because we need them to survive
Because they can bring short‑term joy
questions.explanation: Buying something new releases chemicals in the brain that make us feel better for a little while.

questions.question: What is good to do before shopping, if we feel sad, angry, tired, or very excited?
questions.explanation: Waiting until you are in a neutral mood helps you make more logical financial choices.

questions.question: Does emotional shopping always mean a good decision?
options: Only when it is something we would not want without strong emotions
No, it often involves things we do not need
No, only when we are happy
questions.explanation: Decisions based purely on feelings often lead to regret once the emotion fades.

questions.question: Chrumko is angry and wants to buy a sweet. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Chrumko should wait until he isn't angry anymore to see if he actually wants the sweet.

questions.question: Chrumko is sad and very thirsty and wants to buy water. What should he do?
options: Wait and think about it when he is no longer sad
Not buy anything to save money
Spend all his money on food
questions.explanation: Even if he is sad, thirst is a biological need. He should buy the water because it is a necessity.

questions.question: Chrumko realizes he is not hungry and does not buy anything. Why?
options: He did not need food or anything else
questions.explanation: Chrumko realized that since he wasn't hungry, buying food wasn't a current need.
